Review rating counts for each facet level

Source: R/api-hierarchical-audit.R
facet_small_sample_review.Rd

Reports per-level observation counts, SE, and fit statistics for every level of every facet in a fitted MFRM model, and classifies each level as "sparse", "marginal", "standard", or "strong" using configurable count bands. These labels identify levels to inspect; they do not establish measurement precision or sample adequacy.

Usage

facet_small_sample_review(
  fit,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  thresholds = c(sparse = 10, marginal = 30, standard = 50)
)

Arguments

fit

An mfrm_fit from fit_mfrm().

diagnostics

Optional diagnose_mfrm() output from the same fit. When supplied, per-level Infit and Outfit are added. Estimate and SE come from the fitted facet tables; unavailable SEs remain missing.

thresholds

Named numeric vector of count bands. Defaults are c(sparse = 10, marginal = 30, standard = 50). Supply exactly these three names with finite, positive values satisfying sparse < marginal < standard; their order in the vector is immaterial. The defaults are package screening choices, not precision thresholds.

Value

A list of class mfrm_facet_sample_review with:

  • table: one row per (Facet, Level) with N, Estimate, SE, Infit, Outfit, and SampleCategory.

  • summary: counts of levels in each sample-size category, by facet.

  • facet_summary: count range and lowest count band per facet.

  • thresholds: the applied count bands.

  • notes: count definition and interpretation limits, also shown by print() and summary().

Details

N counts retained rating rows for a level in fit$prep$data, without summing observation weights. For a rater it counts ratings, not distinct examinees; for a person it counts that person's ratings. Repeated or dependent ratings need not supply independent information. Review the counts alongside targeting, connectedness, category use, the estimation method, and available uncertainty estimates before drawing conclusions.

Interpreting output

With the default thresholds, the four labels mean only N < 10, 10 <= N < 30, 30 <= N < 50, and N >= 50, respectively. WorstCategory is the lowest count band represented within a facet. Neither "standard" nor "strong" guarantees narrow intervals, correct coverage, good targeting, or suitability for publication. Do not pool or discard levels solely because of a count label.

Linacre (1994) relates Rasch item/person precision to sample size under targeting and model assumptions. Those guidelines do not establish a precision guarantee for these raw many-facet rating counts. Jones and Wind (2018) study repeated ratings in incomplete designs and highlight examinee precision. Integrating over a population distribution in MML does not remove uncertainty in individual person scores. Interpret SE according to the fitted estimator; this count review adds no interval qualification or hierarchical model.

Typical workflow

  1. Fit with fit_mfrm(); optionally also produce diagnostics with diagnose_mfrm() if you want per-level Infit/Outfit.

  2. Call facet_small_sample_review(fit, diagnostics).

  3. Read the facet_summary first: it highlights the worst level per facet. The summary table gives counts in each band.

  4. If any facet is flagged as sparse or marginal, discuss it in the Methods section; build_apa_outputs() already adds a sentence about the band when fit$summary$FacetSampleSizeFlag is set.

References

Linacre, J. M. (1994). Sample size and item calibration stability. Rasch Measurement Transactions, 7(4), 328. https://rasch.org/rmt/rmt74m.htm

Jones, E., & Wind, S. A. (2018). Using repeated ratings to improve measurement precision in incomplete rating designs. Journal of Applied Measurement, 19(2), 148-161. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29894984/

See also

detect_facet_nesting(), analyze_hierarchical_structure(), compute_facet_icc(), compute_facet_design_effect(), reporting_checklist().

Examples

toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")
fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                method = "MML", quad_points = 7, maxit = 30)
review <- facet_small_sample_review(fit)
summary(review)

strict <- facet_small_sample_review(
  fit,
  thresholds = c(sparse = 15, marginal = 40, standard = 100)
)
strict$facet_summary
